title: Nines without end
hook: 0.999... looks a hair short of 1. Zoom in on the gap and try to find it.

doesNotKnow: that 0.999... names the same number as 1

misconception: 0.999... is a hair less than 1: there is a tiny gap, or a gap that shrinks forever without closing.
objective: The learner can explain that after n nines the gap to 1 is 0.00...01 (one tenth of the previous gap), so with all the nines the gap would have to be smaller than every such number; the only such non-negative number is 0, so 0.999... = 1.

claims.text: With n nines after the point, the gap to 1 is 0.00...01 with n - 1 zeros, that is 1/10^n; each extra nine cuts it to a tenth.
On the stage each new nine zooms in ten times on the gap, so the gap always fills the last tenth of the view.
claims.source: Stage design: the view after n nines spans [1 - 10^-(n-1), 1], ten times narrower than before, and the point 1 - 10^-n sits at 9/10 of it.

claims.text: A gap smaller than every one of 0.1, 0.01, 0.001, ... cannot be positive, so the gap between 0.999... and 1 is 0 and 0.999... = 1.
claims.source: Archimedean property: for any g > 0 there is n with 1/10^n < g. Equivalently the geometric series 9/10 + 9/100 + ... sums to (9/10) / (1 - 1/10) = 1. Any real-analysis text, e.g. Abbott, Understanding Analysis (2nd ed., 2015), sec. 1.4 and 2.7.

claims.text: Three times 0.333... is 0.999..., and three times 1/3 is 1 (shown as a check line on the stage in the 'forever' view).
claims.source: 1/3 = 0.333... (long division); multiplying each digit by 3 has no carries, giving 0.999...; 3 x 1/3 = 1. | v3 2026-10-14 (demo-builder): the check now also appears on the stage ('check: 3 × 0.333… = 0.999…, and 3 × 1/3 = 1') and the reveal points at it. Reopened. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): 1/3 = 0.333... (long division remainder 1 repeats); 3 x 3 = 9 per digit, no carries, so 0.999...; 3 x 1/3 = 1. Stage forever-view check line text matches.

claims.text: The gap went from 0.1 down to 0.00...01, a tenth of the last one per nine. Every gap you named was beaten by enough nines; with all of them, only 0 is left. (Without named gaps the caption reads: Is any positive number below 0.1, 0.01, 0.001... every one? No. Only 0 is.)
claims.source: Same argument as c3 (a positive number r is beaten by 10^-n once n is large enough); the reveal and caption quote the learner's own number of nines, via gap(n) in Demo.tsx (10^-n). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 11): gap(n) = 10^-n (string 0.0..01); for any r > 0 some 10^-n < r (Archimedean), so only 0 is below all of them among non-negatives. Note: the stage says "cut it to a tenth"; the claim paraphrase "one tenth smaller" could read as -10%; the stage wording is the right one. | v3 2026-10-14 (demo-builder): forever-view caption and the reveal now quote the learner's own named gaps (tries in Demo.tsx); the gate needs two named gaps. Reopened. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Demo gap(n) = 10^-n ('0.' + (n-1) zeros + '1'); reveal and caption strings match the claim; Archimedean argument: for r > 0, some 10^-n < r, so no positive number is below every gap.

claims.text: For a named gap 0.0...01 with z zeros after the point (10^-(z+1)), z + 2 nines get closer than that: their gap is 10^-(z+2), e.g. 0.000001 is beaten by 7 nines (gap 0.0000001).
claims.source: With n nines the gap is 10^-n (c1). 10^-n < 10^-(z+1) iff n > z + 1, so the fewest is n = z + 2 (beatenBy in Demo.tsx); with n = z + 1 the gaps are equal, not smaller. Slider range z = 1..30. Added v3 2026-10-14 by demo-builder. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Own check: named(z) = 10^-(z+1); 10^-n < 10^-(z+1) iff n >= z + 2; z = 5: 0.000001 beaten by 7 nines, gap 0.0000001 (named(z+1)). Matches beatenBy() and caption.

recall.question: Is 0.4999... (nines forever after the 4) less than 0.5, or equal to it?
options: Less than 0.5 by a tiny amount
Less than 0.5 by an amount that keeps shrinking
recall.why: The gap would have to be smaller than 0.01, 0.001, 0.0001 and so on, all at once. Only 0 is, so 0.4999... = 0.5.
